the development of an effective and efficient method for the analysis of the parathyroid hormone (PTH) concentration in geriatric (older) cats.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PTH concentration in geriatric renal cats is higher than in younger renal cats and in geriatric healthy cats.
the use of parathyroid hormone (PTH) as a diagnostic test for renal secondary hyperparathyroidism in cats is not warranted.

the use of PTH in the diagnosis of chronic kidney disease in cats is not recommended, but it may be considered in cats that present with hyperphosphatemia, hypocalcemia and a low serum ionized calcium concentration, and that have a low serum creatinine concentration, as these cats are likely to have a low PTH concentration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PTH concentration in cats with renal failure is not only higher than in cats with normal renal function, but is also higher in cats with renal insufficiency than those with chronic renal failure.

the parathyroid hormone (PTH) concentration in cats is significantly higher in cats with chronic renal insufficiency (CRI) than in healthy cats, and that the PTH concentration is higher in cats with moderate to advanced CRI compared to cats with early CRI.
the PTH concentration in cats with renal insufficiency is significantly greater than in cats with regular renal function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parathyroid hormone (PTH) concentration increases with renal failure in cats and that the degree of hyperparathyroidism correlates with severity of chronic renal failure.
cats with CKD have higher PTH concentrations than healthy cats, and cats with stage 1 CKD have higher serum PTH concentrations than cats with stages 2 and 3 CKD.
the serum parathyroid hormone (PTH) concentration is a good indicator of renal function in geriatric cats.
